docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Apart from our Mail-IT-Wize web application, we also offer a RESTful API which provides endpoints for processing, printing documents and envelopes, and finally sending the document to your recipient. The API also has options in place for handling return mail.

Our API can be divided into 2 large components: sending documents along with metadata (Intake request) and consulting previously sent documents (Resource request).

docs.title: Authentication and security
docs.text: All HTTP requests and responses use SSL. Any API requests sent over unencrypted HTTP will not be honoured. These requests will not receive any response, and will time out. For authentication, we use bearer tokens. Send your access token in the Authorization: Bearer [token] header of every request.

docs.title: Managing access tokens
docs.text:
Access tokens are managed by the users, via the API's web portal. These tokens always have a lifetime of 365 days, and are linked to one specific user.

Upon expiration, the API will return an "Unauthenticated" error upon subsequent requests with said token.

An implementation for refreshing tokens/retrieving a new access token via the API itself is under construction.

docs.title: Intake request
docs.text:
Contains the main document, background (optional), envelope (optional), attachments (optional) together with all required metadata (address, recipient, document name, ...)

Important: each intake request contains exactly 1 main document and 1 recipient. To send one PDF to multiple recipients in a single request, use the Bulk Intake request.

docs.title: Resource request
docs.text: A resource request can be used to consult previously sent Intake requests.

docs.title: API base URL and versioning
docs.text:
There is currently a single version available for the API in both UAT and PROD. This is v1.

If a new version is introduced, the previous one will remain active for backwards compatibility. All API users will be notified of new releases.

Base URL for PROD: https://api.mailitwize.be/api/v1

Base URL for UAT: https://api-test.mailitwize.be/api/v1

docs.title: Technical specification
docs.text:
These docs serve as a general introduction and manual for usage of the API.

For more detailed specs on all available API functionality, we suggest also taking a look at our Swagger.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
If you send mail on behalf of your own customers, you can register them as company customers. Each Intake request can then specify the customer it is sent for.

Once we have approved the customer, its name is used as the sender of the printed mail instead of your company's name. For eBox, the eBox configuration set up for that customer is used (see eBox).

docs.title: Managing company customers
docs.text:
Company customers are managed by the users, via the API's web portal, under Company Customers.

Key Description Required Type Default Identifier The value to send in Intake requests. Max. 255 characters, unique within your company YES string Name The customer's name, used as sender. Max. 255 characters YES string Description Free text for your own reference NO string

Once Intakes have been sent for a customer, its identifier can no longer be changed and the customer can no longer be deleted. A customer with an eBox configuration cannot be deleted either.

docs.title: Approval
docs.text:
New customers are inactive until we approve them. When you change the identifier or name of an approved customer, it becomes inactive again until we approve the change.

Intakes can be sent for a customer that awaits approval. They are accepted and linked to the customer as usual, but your company's name is used as sender until the customer is approved. For eBox, see eBox.

docs.title: Customer identifier (optional)
docs.text:
Each Intake request may specify the company customer it is sent for, in its correlation data. This applies to the JSON, Multipart, Bulk, eBox Citizen and eBox Enterprise Intake requests, and to the Estimate requests.

Key Description Required Type Default correlation.customerIdentifier Identifier of the company customer the Intake is sent for (JSON) NO string correlation[customerIdentifier] Identifier of the company customer the Intake is sent for (multipart) NO string

The identifier must be one of your company's customers, approved or not. For a Bulk Intake, the customer applies to every Intake created from it. When omitted, the Intake is sent for your company itself.

Attention

The identifier must be sent as a string. In a JSON request, send "123" rather than 123.

docs.title: eBox
docs.text:
eBox messages are sent with an eBox configuration that we set up for you. If you send eBox messages on behalf of your customers, each customer can have its own eBox configuration, which we link to the customer once it is approved.

The eBox requests also accept the identifier as customer_identifier. It is the same as correlation[customerIdentifier], and either one may be used. When both are sent, they must be equal.

When a customer is specified, the eBox configuration linked to that customer is used. When no customer is specified, your company's own eBox configuration is used, never one linked to a customer.

A customer whose identifier or name was changed keeps its eBox configuration while the change awaits approval, so its messages are still sent. Only a paper fallback uses your company's name as sender until the change is approved.

eBox status updates for a message sent for a customer carry the customer's identifier in customer_identifier.

docs.title: Possible errors
docs.text: HTTP code Description Reason 422 Unprocessable Entity correlation.customerIdentifier is not one of your company's customers, or differs from customer_identifier 400 No eBox configuration eBox only: no eBox configuration is linked to the customer, for example because it is not approved yet

docs.title: Document (required)
docs.text:
Each Bulk Intake request must contain exactly one main document. The document is a PDF file that contains 1 or more recipients.

Key Description Required Type Default document[name] Name of the original document, including extension YES string document[mime-type] MIME type of the document. Currently only "application/pdf" is accepted YES string document[contents] Document PDF file YES file/binary document[multiplex] Print setting of the document. 0 = recto, 1 = recto/verso NO boolean 1

docs.title: Address (required)
docs.text:
Each Bulk Intake request must contain exactly one address location. Coordinates must be specified in points (pts). An address must be present on each page that designates a new recipient, along with a split string (see below).

Key Description Required Type Default address[coordinates][startX] Horizontal starting point of the address box YES number address[coordinates][startY] Vertical starting point of the address box YES number address[coordinates][width] Width of the address box, must be greater than 1 YES number address[coordinates][height] Height of the address box, must be greater than 1 YES number

docs.title: Split string (required)
docs.text:
Each Bulk Intake request must contain exactly one split string location and text. Coordinates must be specified in points (pts). The text in splitString[text] must appear once, on each page that designates a new recipient.

Key Description Required Type Default splitString[coordinates][startX] Horizontal starting point of the split string location YES number splitString[coordinates][startY] Vertical starting point of the split string location YES number splitString[coordinates][width] Width of the split string location, must be greater than 1 YES number splitString[coordinates][height] Height of the split string location, must be greater than 1 YES number splitString[text] The unique text per recipient to split the PDF document on string

Attention

If splitString[text] is not present, the text that is present at the given coordinates on the first page of the document will be set as splitString[text] and used to split the document.

docs.title: Count recipients (required)
docs.text:
Each Bulk Intake request must contain the expected number of recipients. This field will be used to validate against the number of documents that were split based on the splitString parameters.

Key Description Required Type Default count_recipients Amount of expected recipients after splitting Yes integer

Attachments are always printed recto/verso.

docs.title: Success
docs.text:
A successful request will receive the following JSON response (with an HTTP 200 status code):

{
    "bulk_intake_id": 145,
    "status": "received"
}
This indicates the request was well-formed. The file will then be further processed, and updates will be sent via webhooks.

docs.title: Document split result
docs.text:
After a bulk PDF document has been split successfully, we will send back a webhook detailing how many recipients were parsed, on which pages they were found, and the address that was read for each of them.

The cost of the entire bulk is included in cost, as a decimal string with 3 decimals. For partner companies, the cost at partner rates is included as well, in partner_pricing (a number).

{
  "bulk_intake_id": 145,
  "cost": "5.000",
  "created_intakes": [
    {
      "address": {
        "firstname": null,
        "lastname": null,
        "fullname": "John Doe",
        "company": null,
        "street": "Kerkstraat",
        "number": "10",
        "number_alpha": null,
        "box": null,
        "unstructured_street": "",
        "zip": "9800",
        "municipality": "Deinze",
        "country_iso2": "BE",
        "country_name": null
      },
      "first_page": 1,
      "intake_id": 1948,
      "last_page": 2
    }
  ],
  "status": "split",
  "total_recipients": 1
}

Every created Intake then goes through the regular process, and sends its own Intake status updates (Processed, Printing, Shipped, ...) to the same hook[uri].

docs.title: Address validation errors
docs.text:
If any of the parsed addresses in a bulk intake fail validation, these will be sent in a bundled webhook. This webhook will contain the following:

{
  "bulk_intake_id": 145,
  "status": "rejected",
  "data": [
    {
      "first_page": 2,
      "last_page": 2,
      "errors": [
        "houses"
      ],
      "messages": {
        "warnings": [],
        "errors": [
          "You must enter a recipient."
        ],
        "errorCodes": [
          "housesRequired"
        ]
      },
      "parsed_text": "Kerkstraat 10\n9800 Deinze"
    },
    {
      "first_page": 4,
      "last_page": 4,
      "errors": [
        "city",
        "postcode"
      ],
      "messages": {
        "warnings": [],
        "errors": [
          "You must enter a city.",
          "You must enter a zip code."
        ],
        "errorCodes": [
          "cityRequired",
          "postcodeRequired"
        ]
      },
      "parsed_text": "John Doe\nKerkstraat 25"
    }
  ],
  "type": "address_validation_errors"
}
In the data property, we will find all the addresses that failed. The webhook will always include which component of the address caused the failure. parsed_text will always contain the raw text that was parsed on the document.

messages holds a readable message for each error (and any warnings). When a required address component is missing, messages.errorCodes also holds a code per missing component: housesRequired, roadRequired, house_numberRequired, cityRequired or postcodeRequired. When no address could be read at all, errors is ["address"], errorCodes is ["addressRequired"] and parsed_text is empty.

Note: for documents that fail address validation, we will not persist the Intake model to the database. These are only kept in memory at runtime to provide feedback.

docs.title: Possible error codes
docs.text: HTTP code Description Reason 422 Unprocessable Entity Request is invalid - either missing or incorrectly formatted parameters.Refer to validation errors for specifics. 413 Entity Too Large Request size exceeds limit 401 Unauthorized Access token is not valid or expired - refer to the web portal

docs.title: PDF document is not readable
docs.text:
If the transferred PDF document cannot be read, this error will be returned via webhook.

This can occur if the PDF file has been flattened/rasterized, or if the file format has been corrupted.

{
    "bulk_intake_id": 145,
    "status": "error",
    "code": "pdfFileNotReadable",
    "error_message": "The provided PDF file could not be parsed. Verify the file is not corrupted."
}

docs.title: Split text is empty
docs.text:
If no text is found at the split coordinates on the first page, processing is halted and this error will be returned via webhook.

{
    "bulk_intake_id": 145,
    "status": "error",
    "code": "splitTextEmpty",
    "error_message": "Split text at the given coordinates was empty. Processing was halted."
}

docs.title: Amount of split documents does not match count_recipients
docs.text:
If the indicated expected amount of recipients does not match the amount of documents we have after splitting using the identifier, this error will be returned via webhook.

{
    "bulk_intake_id": 145,
    "status": "error",
    "data": {
        "count_recipients": 2,
        "split_count": 6
    },
    "code": "indicatedCountNotEqualsSplitCount",
    "error_message": "Indicated number of recipients does not match the number of intakes. This usually indicates an issue with the splitting identifier."
}

docs.title: Amount of split documents does not match created intakes
docs.text:
If the number of split documents does not match the number of intakes created from them, this error will be returned via webhook.

{
    "bulk_intake_id": 145,
    "status": "error",
    "data": {
        "intakes_count": 5,
        "split_count": 6
    },
    "code": "splitCountNotEqualsDocuments",
    "error_message": "Number of documents does not match the number of expected recipients. This usually indicates an issue with the splitting identifier."
}

All error webhooks share the same structure: bulk_intake_id, status (always error), code, error_message and, for some codes, data.

docs.title: eBox Citizen Multipart Intake Request
docs.text:
Eligibility and access

If you wish to make use of our eBox Citizen service, please contact us at support@mailitwize.be.

Before you can start using this endpoint to send messages to eBox a check needs to be done by BOSA (our eBox Citizen partner) to determine if your organisation is eligible for sending eBox messages.

If you are eligible, we will go through the process together to complete the audit process and enable eBox functionality.

Do note that we have different partners for Citizen and Enterprise, and there are separate procedures to be completed.

docs.title: eBox Hook (optional)
docs.text:
Each Intake request may specify an eBox webhook URL and method to send eBox status updates to: whether the message was offered, delivered and read, or fell back to paper. These are separate from the Intake status updates sent to hook[uri], which only start once a message falls back to paper and its Intake is printed.

Key Description Required Type Default hook_uri URI where the webhook should be sent to. Must be a valid URL. Requires a webhook key (see Webhooks), otherwise a 422 No webhook key found, please set one in your dashboard. is returned YES, if webhook is desired string hook_method HTTP method to be used for the webhook: get, post, GET or POST NO string POST

For more detailed information on eBox status updates, refer to the Webhooks page.

docs.title: Read deadline (optional)
docs.text:
Each Intake request may specify how many days the recipient has to read the message. If the message has been delivered but is not read within that time, it falls back to paper: the Intake is printed and posted, and a fallback webhook with reason messageExpired is sent (see Fallback).

Key Description Required Type Default fallback_days Number of days, counted from the request, to read the message before it falls back to paper. 0 means no deadline NO integer Set by your eBox configuration

When omitted, the deadline from your eBox configuration is used; if that has none either, the message has no deadline and never falls back for not being read. 0 turns the deadline off for this message, even when your eBox configuration has one. The deadline is returned as must_be_read_by in the offered webhook.

docs.title: Customer identifier (optional)
docs.text:
Each Intake request may specify the company customer the eBox message is sent for, with customer_identifier. It is the same as correlation[customerIdentifier]; when both are sent, they must be equal.

Key Description Required Type Default customer_identifier Identifier of the company customer the eBox message is sent for NO string

The eBox configuration linked to that customer is then used. If there is none, a 400 No eBox configuration could be found is returned. When omitted, the eBox configuration of your company is used. An identifier that is not one of your company's customers returns a 422 for correlation.customerIdentifier. See Company Customers for details.

docs.title: Duplicity check (optional)
docs.text:
Each Intake request may specify whether a duplicity check should be run.

The check will determine if another Intake exists with the same document name. If attachments are present, the names of these will also be considered in the check.

If any duplicates are found, a validation error will be returned with a message containing the Intake ID('s) of the duplicate(s).

docs.text:
Eligibility and access

If you wish to make use of our eBox Enterprise service, please contact us at support@mailitwize.be.

Before you can start using this endpoint to send messages to eBox a check needs to be done by the Belgian Social Security (the eBox enterprise service provider) to determine if your organisation is eligible for sending eBox messages.

If you are eligible, we will go through the process together to complete the audit process and enable eBox functionality.

Do note that we have different partners for Citizen and Enterprise, and there are separate procedures to be completed.

docs.title: Read deadline (optional)
docs.text:
Each Intake request may specify how many days the recipient has to read the message. If the message has been delivered but is not read within that time, it falls back to paper: the Intake is printed and posted, and a fallback webhook with reason messageExpired is sent (see Fallback).

When omitted, the deadline from your eBox configuration is used; if that has none either, the message has no deadline and never falls back for not being read. 0 turns the deadline off for this message, even when your eBox configuration has one. The deadline is returned as must_be_read_by in the offered webhook.

An identifier that is not one of your company's customers returns a 422 for correlation.customerIdentifier. See Company Customers for details.

docs.text:
Tip

We recommend the Multipart Intake Request for new integrations. It avoids base64 encoding and is not bound by the 4MB request size limit.

docs.text:
All metadata and documents must be sent in a JSON format. PDF content must be sent in a base-64 encoded string.

Examples for achieving the correct format:

Example

Warning

The maximum size of a JSON request is 4MB! If your payload exceeds this limit, the server will return an HTTP error 413 (entity/payload too large). If you want to send larger documents, use the Multipart Intake request.

docs.title: PHP
docs.text:
<?php
$doc = base64_encode(file_get_contents(‘document.pdf’));

docs.title: C#
docs.text:
String GetBase64FileContent(string fileName, string path)
{
    var file = Directory.GetFiles(path, $"{fileName}.*").FirstOrDefault();
    if (file != null) {
        Byte[] bytes = File.ReadAllBytes(file);
        String base64String = Convert.ToBase64String(bytes);
        return base64String;
    }

    return null;
}

docs.text:
The API will return a JSON response containing the following properties, where previewBase64 contains the final composed PDF file's contents, in a base-64 encoded format. 

{
    "attachmentPages": 6,
    "documentPages": 6,
    "previewBase64": "{base64 encoded string}",
    "totalPages": "18"
}
attachmentPages and documentPages are integers. totalPages is returned as a string.

docs.title: PDF response
docs.text: If the request was sent with an Accept: application/pdf header, the API returns the composed PDF file directly, along with a Content-Type: application/pdf header and a Content-Disposition: inline; filename="{id}.pdf" header, instead of the JSON response above.

docs.title: Possible errors
docs.text: HTTP code Description Reason 401 Unauthorized Access token is not valid or expired - refer to the web portal 403 Forbidden The Intake does not belong to the authenticated user 404 Not Found The Intake file could not be found - it may still be processing

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: For registered mail, we have implemented bpost's Proof of Delivery (POD) API. This allows you to track your registered mail, and optionally download the POD PDF document.

docs.title: Endpoint and method
docs.text: There are 2 endpoints available for the POD's: retrieving POD information and downloading the POD document (if available).

docs.title: Request POD information
docs.text: API version v1 Endpoint base_url/api_version/proof-of-delivery/{id} Method GET

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
{
    "podGuid": "string",
    "podBusinessKey": "miw2_",
    "requestDateTime": "2024-03-20T14:00:00+00:00",
    "barcode": "JJBEA000000000000012345",
    "deliveryStates": [
        {
            "stateCode": "PodDownloadRequestPodInfoSucceeded",
            "stateDisplaytext": "Pod download request, pod info succeeded",
            "transitionDateTime": "2023-08-01T10:00:00+02:00"
        }
    ],
    "documentInfo": {
        "hasPodAvailable": true,
        "hasOriginalDocumentAvailable": true
    }
}

docs.title: Download POD document
docs.text:
Attention

This will only work if the hasPodAvailable parameter from the information request is true.

API version v1 Endpoint base_url/api_version/proof-of-delivery/{id}/document Method POST

docs.title: Response
docs.text: The POD document will be returned as binary, with an application/pdf header.

docs.title: Possible errors
docs.text:
Both POD endpoints can return:

HTTP code Description Reason 403 Forbidden The Intake does not belong to the authenticated user

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Once a request has been accepted by the API, status updates can be sent to you via webhooks. There are three kinds:

Kind Sent for Configured with Intake status updates Every Intake, including eBox ones once they are printed hook.uri / hook.method (hook[uri] / hook[method]) eBox status updates eBox Citizen and eBox Enterprise messages hook_uri / hook_method Bulk Intake updates Bulk Intakes hook[uri] / hook[method], see Bulk Intake

Webhooks are only sent when you specify a URI in the request. The method is POST unless you specify GET (get, post, GET or POST are accepted).

docs.title: Webhook key
docs.text:
To make use of webhooks, you will need to generate a webhook key in the web portal first, under Webhook. Every webhook is signed with this key. A request that specifies a webhook URI while your company has no webhook key is rejected with a 422 No webhook key found, please set one in your dashboard.

On the same page you can optionally set an API key. When set, it is sent along with every webhook in an X-API-Key header, for receivers that require one.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
Each webhook is sent with the following headers:

Header Value Content-Type application/json Signature HMAC-SHA256 of the JSON payload, using your webhook key, hex encoded X-API-Key Your API key, only when one is set in the web portal

With POST (the default), the payload is sent as the JSON request body.

With GET, the same payload is sent as query string parameters instead (nested values in key[subkey]=value notation), and all values arrive as strings. We recommend POST: see the note on verifying GET webhooks below.

docs.title: Verifying the signature
docs.text:
Calculate the HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, using the webhook key as key. If it matches the value of the Signature header, the payload is valid.

For example, in PHP: 

<?php
$jsonPayload = file_get_contents('php://input');
$hash = hash_hmac('sha256', $jsonPayload, $webhookKey);
if (hash_equals($hash, $_SERVER['HTTP_SIGNATURE'])) {
    // Payload contents verified
    // ...
}

Warning

Always calculate the signature over the body exactly as it was received. Decoding and re-encoding the JSON first will usually give a different result: slashes are sent escaped (\/) and non-ASCII characters as \uXXXX.

For GET webhooks there is no body: the signature is calculated over the payload encoded as JSON in the same way, which you would have to reconstruct from the query string. Use POST if you want to verify webhooks.

docs.title: Delivery and retries
docs.text:
A webhook counts as delivered when your endpoint responds with an HTTP 2xx status code within 3 seconds. Otherwise it is retried, up to 3 attempts in total: the second attempt follows after about 10 seconds, the third after about 100 seconds. After the third failed attempt the webhook is dropped and not sent again.

A webhook can arrive more than once (for example when your endpoint processed it but responded too late), and webhooks are not guaranteed to arrive in the order they were sent. Respond quickly and process the payload afterwards, and make your processing safe to repeat.

docs.title: Intake status updates
docs.text:
These are sent to hook.uri with hook.method, as specified in the Intake request.

Currently, there are 5 possible Intake status updates:

Status Sent when Processed The Intake was received and processed by our server, and is waiting to be printed. Not sent for eBox Intakes Printing The Intake was processed and put on the print queue. For eBox Intakes, only after a fallback to paper Shipped The Intake was printed and handed to bpost for delivery Rejected The Intake was rejected by our print production. Not enabled by default, see below Returned The postal item was returned to Symeta Hybrid. Not enabled by default, see below

Info

The payloads below are exactly as sent. Note that the casing of status differs (rejected is lowercase), and that not every payload has data and type.

The payloads are as follows, for each status:

docs.title: Processed
docs.text:
{
    "intake": 158056,
    "status": "Processed",
    "data": ""
}

docs.title: Printing
docs.text:
{
    "intake": 158056,
    "status": "Printing"
}

docs.title: Shipped
docs.text:
{
    "intake": 158056,
    "status": "Shipped",
    "data": {
        "bpost": "JJBEA000000000000012345", 
        "shipping_date": "15-03-2024"
    },
    "type": "status_update"
}

docs.title: Rejected
docs.text:
This webhook is not automatically enabled. If you wish to have this activated for your intakes, please contact us at support@mailitwize.be.

{
    "intake": 158056,
    "status": "rejected",
    "data": {
        "rejected_reason": "string"
    },
    "type": "status_update"
}

docs.title: Returned
docs.text:
This webhook is not automatically enabled. If you wish to have this activated for your intakes, please contact us at support@mailitwize.be.

{
    "intake": 158056,
    "status": "Returned",
    "data": {
        "barcode": "JJBEA000000000000012345",
        "reasonCode": "S11",
        "reasonDescription": "Ontvangt de briefwisseling niet op aangeduid adres",
        "scanned_at": "2024-03-17 12:00:00"
    },
    "type": "status_update"
}

docs.title: eBox status updates
docs.text:
These are sent to hook_uri with hook_method, as specified in the eBox Citizen or eBox Enterprise request. They report on the eBox message. The paper Intake that comes with it reports separately, through the Intake status updates sent to hook[uri].

Currently, there are 4 possible eBox status updates:

Status Sent when offered The message was published to the recipient's eBox delivered eBox confirmed the message is available to the recipient read The recipient opened the message fallback The message will be sent on paper instead, see Fallback

Every eBox status update contains the following keys:

Key Description Always present message Unique identifier (GUID) of the eBox message: the message returned by the eBox request, or the guid you sent YES type Always status_update YES status One of offered, delivered, read or fallback YES data Details of the status, see the payloads below YES ebox_status The event as reported by eBox itself, when the update was triggered by one NO customer_identifier The customer the message was sent for, when it was sent for one of your company customers NO

Date and time formats

offered_at is sent in ISO 8601 format, in UTC. must_be_read_by is sent as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmm. All other timestamps are sent as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS without a timezone offset: Belgian local time (Europe/Brussels), except for expires_at and the times of events reported by eBox, which keep the timezone eBox reported them in.

The payloads are as follows, for each status:

docs.title: Offered
docs.text:
{
    "message": "8f0c2a6e-2b8e-4a39-9d6f-3c1f2f6e9a10",
    "type": "status_update",
    "status": "offered",
    "data": {
        "expires_at": "2027-10-29 10:14:00",
        "must_be_read_by": "2026-11-28 10:14:00.000",
        "offered_at": "2026-10-29T09:14:00.000000Z"
    }
}
Key Description expires_at The expiration date eBox gave the message must_be_read_by Deadline by which the message must be read before it falls back to paper (see Fallback), or null when there is no deadline offered_at When the eBox request was received by the API

docs.title: Delivered
docs.text:
For a message sent for one of your company customers, customer_identifier is included, as in this example.

{
    "message": "8f0c2a6e-2b8e-4a39-9d6f-3c1f2f6e9a10",
    "type": "status_update",
    "status": "delivered",
    "data": {
        "delivered_at": "2026-10-29 10:15:00"
    },
    "ebox_status": "newDocument",
    "customer_identifier": "customer-001"
}

docs.title: Read
docs.text:
{
    "message": "8f0c2a6e-2b8e-4a39-9d6f-3c1f2f6e9a10",
    "type": "status_update",
    "status": "read",
    "data": {
        "read_at": "2026-10-30 18:02:11"
    },
    "ebox_status": "readDocument"
}

docs.title: Fallback
docs.text:
When a message cannot be delivered digitally, it falls back to paper: the Intake sent with the eBox request is printed and posted like any other Intake, and reports through the Intake status updates (Printing, Shipped, ...) on hook[uri]. A message falls back at most once.

{
    "message": "8f0c2a6e-2b8e-4a39-9d6f-3c1f2f6e9a10",
    "type": "status_update",
    "status": "fallback",
    "data": {
        "fallback_at": "2026-11-28 10:20:00",
        "fallback_reason": "messageExpired"
    }
}
fallback_reason ebox_status Reason failedToSend (absent) The message could not be published to eBox noDigitalCitizen noDigitalCitizen eBox Citizen: eBox reports the recipient cannot receive the message digitally noDigitalConsumer noDigitalConsumer eBox Citizen: eBox reports the recipient cannot receive the message digitally newDocumentOnPaper newDocumentOnPaper eBox Citizen: eBox reports the message is to be delivered on paper noDigitalEnterprise noDigitalEnterprise eBox Enterprise: eBox accepted the message, but the recipient enterprise has no digital eBox enterpriseNotFullDigital (absent) eBox Enterprise: the recipient enterprise does not receive its mail exclusively through eBox messageExpired (absent) The message was delivered but not read before must_be_read_by

The read deadline (must_be_read_by) is set by fallback_days in the eBox request, or else by your eBox configuration (see Read deadline). When there is no deadline, a message that is delivered but never read does not fall back.

docs.title: eBox Citizen
docs.text:
1. offered once the message is published.
  2. delivered once eBox reports the message as available (newDocument).
  3. read once the recipient opens it (readDocument). The paper Intake is then discarded and will not be printed.

docs.title: eBox Enterprise
docs.text:
1. offered once the message is published, immediately followed by delivered: for eBox Enterprise a published message is available to the recipient right away.
  2. If the recipient enterprise does not receive its mail exclusively through eBox, a fallback with reason enterpriseNotFullDigital follows. The message stays in the recipient's eBox, and is also sent on paper.
  3. read once the recipient opens it (readDocument). If no fallback happened, the paper Intake is discarded and will not be printed.

A fallback is not necessarily the last update: eBox may still report a message as delivered or read after it has fallen back.
